subsystems.name: Entanglement sources
subsystems.role: produce pairs of photons whose quantum states are correlated.
parts: nonlinear crystals for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Quantum memories
subsystems.role: hold a qubit's state long enough for a network to synchronise.

subsystems.name: Repeater nodes
subsystems.role: extend range past fibre loss by swapping entanglement segment by segment.

subsystems.name: End nodes
subsystems.role: small quantum processors that store, manipulate and read out entanglement.

subsystems.name: Classical control plane
subsystems.role: synchronises clocks, reports successful links and routes entanglement.

buildSteps.title: Generate entangled photons
buildSteps.detail: A laser pumps a nonlinear crystal or a quantum dot, emitting photon pairs in an entangled state.

buildSteps.title: Shift to telecom wavelength
buildSteps.detail: Photons are converted to wavelengths around 1550 nm so they survive the least-lossy fibre window.

buildSteps.title: Send down fibre or free space
buildSteps.detail: Pairs travel through installed fibre, or via satellite for intercontinental links.

buildSteps.title: Catch and store
buildSteps.detail: At a repeater or end node, a photon is absorbed into a quantum memory and its arrival is heralded.

buildSteps.title: Swap to extend range
buildSteps.detail: A node performs a joint measurement on two stored photons, transferring entanglement between distant partners; a classical signal confirms success.

buildSteps.title: Link to processors
buildSteps.detail: Photons are entangled with matter qubits in small processors, so computation can happen on the stored state.

buildSteps.title: Repeat and route
buildSteps.detail: Chains of swaps connect distant nodes, and a control plane routes entanglement requests across the network.

buildSteps.title: Run an application
buildSteps.detail: Users consume entanglement for quantum key distribution, distributed algorithms or blind computation without exposing their data.

prerequisites.why: entanglement has been shared over hundreds of kilometres of fibre and via satellite, proving the basic channel.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum memories with high efficiency and long coherence
prerequisites.why: storage times and read-out fidelities improved a lot but still limit swap rates.
demonstrated in small multi-node testbeds, not yet chained across a real network.
superconducting processors work at microwave frequencies and need conversion to telecom photons to link to fibre.
a useful quantum internet needs many logical qubits per node, which today's hardware cannot yet supply.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point entanglement links and trusted-node metropolitan key networks; satellite entanglement demonstrated by the Micius mission in 2017
pathway.unlocks: secure key distribution and proof that photons survive long links.

pathway.milestone: three-node repeater networks with memories, such as the Delft demonstration in 2021
pathway.unlocks: the building block for a true repeater chain.

pathway.milestone: metropolitan quantum networks connecting two or more small processors
pathway.unlocks: distributed quantum computing and networked sensing.

pathway.milestone: intercity and intercontinental links using satellites and repeaters, integrated with error-corrected processors
pathway.unlocks: a general quantum internet with applications that cannot be replicated classically.
